title: When you're not feeling well
title_target: ឈឺខ្លួន — chheu khluèn
goal: Name parts of the body and describe symptoms at a pharmacy or clinic — with the Khmer pattern that makes the body part the object, not the subject.
bekal: name the body parts people complain about most
describe a symptom with ខ្ញុំឈឺ + body part
tell ឈឺ, គ្រុនក្តៅ, រាគ, ក្អួត apart
ask for medicine at a pharmacy
mention allergies and call for help in an emergency

dialogs.title: កិច្ចសន្ទនា — At the pharmacy near the market
dialogs.intro: Back from Siem Reap, Ani has stomach trouble. Watch how the complaints are built: not "my head hurts" but "I hurt head" — the body part is the object.

grammars.title: ⚠️ ឈឺ + body part — "I hurt head"
body: English says "my head hurts" (the head is the subject) or "I have a headache". Khmer says **"I hurt head"** — the person is the subject and the body part is the object. Get this order into your head early and don't flip it.

Literally
Translation
rows: ខ្ញុំឈឺក្បាល

after: ⚠️ ក្បាលខ្ញុំឈឺ is also understood, but it sounds translated. The natural form, and the one you'll always hear from Cambodians, is ខ្ញុំឈឺក្បាល.
**ឈឺ also means "sick" in general**: ខ្ញុំឈឺ means "I'm sick". For something more serious, people say ឈឺធ្ងន់ (*chheu thngun*, "seriously ill").

grammars.title: Four complaints you mustn't mix up
body: Khmer uses completely different words for four conditions that a learner might lump together as "being sick". Mixing them up could get you the wrong medicine.

head: Khmer
Say it
Meaning
rows: អស់កម្លាំង

after: ⚠️ Notice **វិលមុខ** (dizzy) and **ឈឺក្បាល** (headache) — two different things, and mixing them up is a very common mistake. វិលមុខ means the world is spinning; ឈឺក្បាល means your head aches.

grammars.title: ដង — counting how many times
body: ដង (*daang*) is the classifier for **occurrences**, like English "times". The pattern is the same as other classifiers: number + ដង.

head: Khmer
Say it
Translation
rows: បីដងមួយថ្ងៃ

after: ⚠️ "Once" is **ម្តង** (*mdaang*), not មួយដង. It's the only number that merges into a special form; two times and up are regular again. ម្តង also means "for a moment" in requests: មើលម្តង ("have a look").

blocks.title: ⚠️ Three practical tips for newcomers to Cambodia
items: **Pharmacies are much less strict than in many countries.** Lots of medicines that need a prescription elsewhere can be bought over the counter. That's convenient, but it also means you need to know what you're taking — describe your symptoms clearly and ask what the medicine is called.

**For serious illness, there are international clinics in Phnom Penh and Siem Reap.** The sentence ខ្ញុំត្រូវការគ្រូពេទ្យនិយាយភាសាអង់គ្លេស ("I need a doctor who speaks English") is worth having ready.

**Dengue and malaria are real in the rainy season.** If a fever doesn't go down within two days, don't wait — ទៅមន្ទីរពេទ្យ. The words ឈាម (*chhiem*, blood) and គ្រុនឈាម (dengue fever) are worth knowing.
